## p146 A — Repeat order placing radio stations under officer control

**Edition context:** Kiel radio-control order — p140 A and p146 A.

**Related source pages:** [p140 A1](140.md#source-p140-a1), [p140 A2](140.md#source-p140-a2), [p140 A3](140.md#source-p140-a3), [p140 A4](140.md#source-p140-a4).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-kiel-radio-control-kiel-radio-control-order--p140-a-and-p146-a"></a>



**Prior interpretation: J. Rives Childs; George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Source comparison and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four-part order instructs radio stations to come under an officer's immediate control, prevent the reception and distribution of messages from Kiel, and confiscate and destroy texts already received. Its historical interpretation and the p146 repeat were already described in [section 6.4 of Lasry et al.](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p23. The present edition adds literal source transcriptions, independently checked coordinate arithmetic, and an explicit repair of the repeated first part.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-kiel-radio-control-readable-text"></a>

### Readable text

**Readable German:**

> Sämtliche Funkstellen sofort durch Offizier fest in Hand nehmen. Verhindern, dass Funksprüche aus Kiel, Kiel aufgenommen und verbreitet werden. Bereits aufgenommene Texte beschlagnahmen und vernichten. Größte Eile geboten. Nachrchef, röm. vier, V, 47?00, geh.

The wording is an editorial reading. The repeated **Kiel, Kiel** is retained. The reference `47?00` remains incomplete; the displayed uncertainty is not permission to choose any digit independently of its coordinate domain.

p140 A is headed `YZ NKJ v LP (3.52 p.m., November 6th)`, `1331 (6/11) 4 TEILE`. The first part reappears in p146 A, headed `ASO v NKJ (04.19 a.m., November 7th)` and `WH BIS 0025 30 GR 1331 (KR)`. Both use the published **Nov4–6** key. The later interception date does not imply that the repeat was re-encrypted under the next key.

| Record | Source slots / advertised | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Changes for the displayed reading |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| p140 A1 | 112 / 112 | 56/56 | 2 known-coordinate substitutions |
| p140 A2 | 134 / 134 | 65/67 | 3 substitutions and 2 erasure fills |
| p140 A3 | 102 / 102 | 47/51 | 2 substitutions and 4 erasure fills |
| p140 A4 | 98 / 98 | 45/49 | 3 substitutions and 3 fills; number remains unresolved |
| p146 A | 117 / 112 | 51/56 after the declared five-slot deletion | 1 substitution and 5 fills |

p146 A is a separate record from the challenge's **p146 B**, whose duplicated `XAAXV` group has its [own case](#edition-cases-p146).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-kiel-radio-control-repeated-first-part-an-extra-group-and-a-witnessed-letter"></a>

### Repeated first part: an extra group and a witnessed letter

p146 prints **117 slots** despite its `RICHI-112` label. Its twelfth group, `VAADX`, is absent from p140. Removing that group yields a 112-slot stream with only two disagreements at known coordinates against p140. Screening every contiguous five-slot deletion gives the same minimum at zero-based starts **54 and 55**; the two deletions produce an identical stream because of a repeated boundary `X`. Both aliases are preserved in the certificate.

The resulting literal decryptions are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — p146 uses the stated duplicate-group deletion; p140 is separate:**

```text
p140 A1
SAEMTLICHEFUNKSTELLENSOFORTDURCHO1FIGIERFESTINHANDNEHMEN

p146 A after the declared deletion
SAEMTL?CHEFUNKS?ELLE?SOFORTDURCHOFFIFIERFEST?NHANDNE?MEN
```

</details>

Across the two copies, **55 of the 56 positions** in the readable first part are witnessed directly. The later copy supplies the first `F` in `OFFIZIER`, where p140 gives `1`. The letter `Z` remains an editorial correction: p140 gives `G` and p146 gives `F` at that position. Thus the repeat improves the text without turning every proposed letter into observed evidence.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-kiel-radio-control-other-raw-parts"></a>

## p146 — Kerch radio call-sign instruction

**Edition context:** p146 — Kerch radio call-sign instruction.

<a id="edition-cases-p146-p146--kerch-radio-call-sign-instruction"></a>



The Kerch radio station is assigned the call sign Richard–Emil–Karl. Our duplicate-group reconstruction of the Nov4–6-key message fixes **117 of 122 positions** while retaining all 239 coordinates outside the duplicated group unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-p146-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — reconstructed frame and word repairs stated below:**

> Funkstelle Kertsch erhaelt ab 12.[11] Rufnamen Richard Emil Karl. Funkstellen dortigen Bereichs benachrichtigen. Nachrichtenchef 4BG7834.

**Meaning:** The Kerch radio station is to use the call sign spelled out as Richard–Emil–Karl from the stated date, most plausibly 12 November. Notify the radio stations in that area. The closing administrative reference remains literal.

The conditional model removes one of two identical `XAAXV` groups and restores a missing five-coordinate group. The proposed fill `AAXAA` supplies `L, 1, N, E, F` in the reading. Its month digit is `1` under the ordinary day.month interpretation of `12.1?`.

<a id="edition-cases-p146-duplicate-group-repair"></a>

### Duplicate-group repair

The [source image](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p146_B.png) prints `XAAXV XAAXV XAFDX` near the end. Removing either identical copy and leaving the five-coordinate gap unfilled gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional removal of one duplicate group and retention of an unfilled five-coordinate gap:**

```text
FUNKSTELLEKERTSCHERHAE?TAB12X1?XRUFNAME?RICHARD?MILKARLX?UNKSTELLENDORTIGENBEREICHSBENACHRICHTIGENXNACHRICHTENCHEF4BG7834X
```

</details>

The five unresolved domains permit 7,776 strings. The proposed completion follows the words and date convention; the final administrative reference remains literal.

The [new certificate](../../data/certificates/p146_duplicate_group.json) retains all eighteen insertion/deletion alignments compatible with the chosen full reading. Only two alignments use printed five-letter group boundaries, corresponding to deletion of either duplicate. [Independent review](../../data/reviews/p146_duplicate_independent.json) confirms the arithmetic and the source glyphs. The [repair report](../../experiments/source_recovery/README.md) compares the new model with Norbert's earlier reconstruction.

The duplicate-group repair and source review are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. [Norbert's 1 March 2017 reading](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852664) established the body and missing-group approach. Baertl's alternative `ERHATBETRIEB` wording is retained in the comparison below.

## 6 November Ringbahn-key instruction to Tiflis

<a id="november-6-ringbahn-key-instruction-to-tiflis"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p146 C1, p146 C2.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-november-6-ringbahn-key-instruction-to-tiflis"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two-part **section C on Childs p146** tells the Caucasus delegation at
Tiflis to retain November Ringbahn keys and use them for the beginning of
December. Its schedule agrees with independently readable spans in the
[p145 instruction](145.md#edition-cases-radio-nov6-ringbahn-key-witnesses) and
[p211 lower-B instruction](211.md#edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule), but this dispatch has its
own wording, address and part boundaries. The original
[p146 challenge](#edition-cases-p146) is section B; these are two different physical
records.

The literal source contains **365 slots**, including six masked coordinates,
against **368 advertised**. The conditional frames insert three unknown
coordinate slots and produce **184 plaintext positions, 175 fixed before
word repairs**. The complete proposed reading uses **1 observed-coordinate
substitution, 6 source-mask fills and 3 inserted-slot fills**. No printed
slot is deleted or reordered and the published **Nov4–6** key is unchanged.
The insertion positions and complete wording remain stated hypotheses.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p146_C_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/sources/p146_C_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

<a id="source-p146-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-p146-c1"></a>

### p146 C1

Part 1 prints **174 valid coordinates** and advertises **176**. Its `XAAF`
group at source indices 65–68 is visibly short. The displayed frame inserts
one unknown at **source boundary 66** and another at **source boundary 173**.
A boundary is before the original source index of that number. Consequently,
the inserted slots have **model indices 66 and 174**; original source indices
do not shift in the transcription.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 176-slot frame; 86/88 fixed positions:**

```text
RINGBAHNNOVEMBERSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENX?CHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTE?NOVEMBERUSWX
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 0 observed-coordinate substitutions, 0 source-mask fills and 2 inserted-slot fills; 88/88 fixed positions:**

```text
RINGBAHNNOVEMBERSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXSCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWX
```

</details>

| Added source boundary | Model index | Supplied coordinate | Plaintext position supplied |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 66 | 66 | G | 42, S in SCHLUESSEL |
| 173 | 174 | A | 75, R in ZEHNTER |

The first fill changes the short group from `XAAF` to `XGAAF` in the model.
The second adds a coordinate before the final printed `D`; that location is
inferred from the cipher comparison, not a visible blank. Neither fill is
counted as a change to an observed coordinate.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Ringbahn-Novemberschluessel nicht vernichten. Schluessel erster Dezember wie zehnter November usw.

**Meaning:** Keep the November Ringbahn keys; use the 10 November key for
1 December, and continue in the stated sequence.

The exact complete candidate is encrypted and compared against the literal
174-slot source under **all 15,400 ways of inserting two slots**. There is
exactly **one zero-substitution alignment** for that fixed candidate: source
boundaries 66 and 173. The certificate records the cost histogram and the
minimum. This establishes a precise compatibility result within the declared
family. It does not prove that every possible plaintext has been excluded,
or identify when the historical omissions occurred.

<a id="source-p146-c2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-p146-c2"></a>

### p146 C2

Part 2 prints **191 source slots**, of which **185 are valid coordinates**,
and advertises **192**. The first-line group `VF--` at source indices 35–38
is visibly four slots long. For the displayed raw output, one unknown slot
is inserted at **source boundary 37**. The literal two dashes, the two dashes
in the following `VF--X`, the `W` in `FXXDW`, and the dash in `-DGVD` all
remain source observations.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 192-slot frame; 89/96 fixed positions:**

```text
BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBERWI?DREISSIG?TERNO?E?BERXEMPFANGS?ESTAETIGUNGX?A8HRICH?ENCHEF4B47857X
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 1 observed-coordinate substitution, 6 source-mask fills and 1 inserted-slot fill; 96/96 fixed positions:**

```text
BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBERWIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBERXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B47857X
```

</details>

The sole observed-coordinate substitution is **source 132 V→X**, supplying
`C` in the proposed word `NACHRICHTENCHEF` where the raw output has `8`.
No numeral elsewhere is relabeled. The complete repair account for the
boundary-37 display frame is:

| Kind | Source index or boundary | Model index | Value supplied |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Added-slot fill | Boundary 37 | 37 | A |
| Printed dash fill | 37 | 38 | X |
| Printed dash fill | 38 | 39 | F |
| Printed dash fill | 41 | 42 | X |
| Printed dash fill | 42 | 43 | A |
| Invalid printed W fill | 108 | 109 | V |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 132 | 133 | V→X |
| Printed dash fill | 174 | 175 | G |

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Bis einundzwanzigster Dezember wie dreissigster November. Empfangsbestaetigung. Nachrichtenchef 4B47857.

**Meaning:** Continue through 21 December using the 30 November key, and
acknowledge receipt. The trailing reference **4B47857** is literal under the
published square; its historical numerical assignment is not independently
established here.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-equal-cost-gap-alternatives"></a>

#### Equal-cost gap alternatives

The verifier tests **all 192 single-gap positions** against the same complete
candidate. Three positions tie at the minimum cost of one observed-coordinate
substitution:

| Source boundary | Added coordinate | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Inserted-slot fills |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 37 | A | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| 38 | X | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| 39 | F | 1 | 6 | 1 |

All three produce the same displayed raw and edited plaintext. They differ
in which part of the restored `VFAXF` group is attributed to the missing slot
and which to the two printed masks. The certificate preserves each mapping
and its complete repair events. **Boundary 37 is the presentation choice;
the evidence does not distinguish these three gap positions.**
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-source-and-date-layers"></a>

### Source and date layers

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — headers and cleartext annotation:**

```text
Page heading: 6th NOVEMBER, 1918.
C) COS v LP (06.46 a.m., November 7th)
FUER COS 2040 (6/11) AN NACHRICHTENKOMMDR KAUKASUS DELEGATION
TIFLIS 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-176
2 TL RICHI-192
Cleartext ending after part 2: NKJ v LP UM
```

</details>

The dispatch date in the heading and address line is 6 November; the
intercept line says 7 November. These layers are retained. The separately
printed `NKJ v LP UM` follows the second ciphertext and is not an extra
coordinate group. Exact grouped ciphertext, including every dash and the
invalid printed `W`, is preserved in the
[inputs](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-independent-support-and-limits"></a>

### Independent support and limits

The verifier independently decodes pinned source rows from the earlier
editions, rather than treating their edited prose as direct evidence:

| New proposed span | Independently fixed raw source |
| --- | --- |
| SCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSW | p211 lower B2 |
| BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBER | p211 lower B2 |
| WIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBER | p145 B3 |
| EMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNG | p145 B3 |

These matches directly support the missing schedule letters in C1 and the
schedule/acknowledgment fills in C2. The final `NACHRICHTENCHEF` is a separately
priced lexical restoration from `?A8HRICH?ENCHEF`; the other dispatches print
the shorter `NACHRCHEF` and do not by themselves supply this expanded word.
All three repairs in that word remain editorial.

The new instruction begins `RINGBAHNNOVEMBER` and does not reproduce the
other dispatch's separate sentence postponing the December key. These
records are not merged into one purported identical copy. The agreement
supports the transmitted schedule, without demonstrating that every
station followed it or assigning a key to any particular December message.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-tiflis-ringbahn-instruction-attribution-and-reproduction"></a>

### Attribution and reproduction

The source is J. Rives Childs's *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*. Published period-key recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's 2017 key list, and the already published p145
and p211 editions retain their original credit. Earlier repository OCR is
frozen with recomputed unchanged-key outputs: it separated the first row
of C1 and then merged the remainder of C1 with C2. The current work restores
the physical source frames and makes the word repairs reviewable. It makes
**no first-decipherment claim**.

[Inputs and literal source](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json),

provide every position domain, source/model map, exact re-encryption,
independent supporting span and gap-search boundary.
